fields.Short Description: Boat tours of Winyah Bay, the rice plantations and Shell Island. Call to confirm the departure dock.
fields.Hours Note: Book online. In summer, book about two weeks ahead. Tours leave from 701 Front St, Georgetown.
fields.Name: Cap'n Rod's Lowcountry Tours

fields.Short Description: Boat tours from the Georgetown harbor. Address needs confirming.
fields.Name: Rover Boat Tours

fields.Short Description: A historic lowcountry rice plantation house open for tours. The circa-1740 house is seen on a guided tour of about 50 minutes that covers the lives of both the owners and the enslaved people who lived and worked there. Tours run on the hour Tuesday through Saturday, and online booking is available. The riverside grounds overlook the North Santee River.
fields.Hours Note: House tours on the hour. Tours are for ages 6 and up.
fields.Name: Hopsewee Plantation

fields.Short Description: Maritime history on the Georgetown waterfront, with free admission. Exhibits cover South Carolina's maritime past, including a Fresnel lens from the old North Island lighthouse and bricks salvaged from the c. 1730 Brown's Ferry Vessel, along with changing displays and a gift shop. Open Monday through Saturday.
fields.Name: South Carolina Maritime Museum

fields.Short Description: The Franklin G. Burroughs-Simeon B. Chapin Art Museum shows rotating art exhibitions on South Ocean Boulevard, across from the beach.
fields.Address: 3100 S Ocean Blvd, Myrtle Beach, SC 29577
fields.Name: Myrtle Beach Art Museum

fields.Short Description: Exhibits on nearly 300 years of local history, from colonial beginnings and the Revolutionary era to the indigo, rice, lumber and paper industries and today's tourism economy. The museum also houses the Francis Marion Interpretive Center and has a gift shop. The building has an entrance ramp and an elevator to the second floor. Free admission.
fields.Name: Georgetown County Museum

fields.Short Description: Local history museum in Conway, a short drive inland.
fields.Name: Horry County Museum

fields.Short Description: The Moorish-style winter home of Archer and Anna Hyatt Huntington, inside Huntington Beach State Park. Visitors can explore the castle for a small separate fee on top of park entry. Pair it with the beach, birding and the freshwater lake in the same park.
fields.Hours Note: Open until 5 PM during Daylight Saving Time. May close for large events.
fields.Price: $2 per person ages 6+, plus state park admission ($8 adults, $4 ages 6–15)
fields.Address: Huntington Beach State Park, 16148 Ocean Hwy, Murrells Inlet, SC 29576
fields.Name: Atalaya Castle

fields.Short Description: A downtown true-crime museum created by profiler Phil Chalmers, with case artifacts and a look at how investigators build a profile. Aimed at adults.
fields.Name: Serial Killers: The Experience

fields.Short Description: A museum and education center telling the story of the 1932 school that served the area's Black students for more than two decades, rebuilt in 2006 with help from former students.
fields.Name: Historic Myrtle Beach Colored School Museum

fields.Short Description: A historic house museum on the Sampit River.
fields.Name: Kaminski House Museum

fields.Short Description: The story of Georgetown's rice culture in the old Market Building. The museum also has the Prevost Art Gallery for local art, a shop of local makers' goods, books and culinary items, and occasional workshops such as indigo dyeing. Open Tuesday through Saturday; check the website for current hours.
fields.Name: Rice Museum

fields.Short Description: A collection of vintage American cars and trucks, including the original Charger Daytona from the movie Joe Dirt.
fields.Name: Wheels of Yesteryear

fields.Short Description: Lantern-lit ghost walks through the historic district, Friday evenings at dusk by reservation. Call for the meeting point.
fields.Hours Note: Friday evenings at dusk, by reservation only (at least five adults). Times change with the season.
fields.Name: Ghosts of Georgetown Lantern Tours
